description:

Email from Michael on 11/10/22
While automated tests (S4.4.0.24, S4SP 3.0.3113, USB3 box, AE sensor size 1) last night I saw the following issue: 
A bitewing series was started. 2 out of 4 exposures were performed successfully. After that the 3rd {*}box flashes red but never changes to the green state though the hardware shows flashing green led{*}.
On releasing xray, the image is captured as expected and shown in the acquisition UI (Sidexis). Also the next empty box flashes green (as expected).

• Though when the sensor is exposed, the image is acquired and shown in the box. 
• After that exposure, the next box is set to flashing green as expected.

This time a full mouth series (21) was affected. So it seems independent on the exposure type.

For me it seems to appear in ~ 1/500 exposures. I hope you have more information for us and at best a hint how to resolve that issue.

summary: Unexpected Orange Residue Present on Electronic Chips of USB3 Interfaces After Manufacturing
description:
During inspection of manufactured USB3 Interfaces, an orange-colored spot/residue was observed on the electronic chips of most devices. Based on the expected manufacturing quality standards, this orange residue should not be present on the chip surfaces. *Actual Result:*
 * An orange-colored spot/residue is visible on the electronic chips of the majority of manufactured USB3 Interfaces.
 * The residue appears directly on electronic components where such material is not expected.
 * The cause and potential impact on product quality, reliability, or functionality are unknown.

*Expected Result:*
 * Electronic chips on manufactured USB3 Interfaces should be free of any unexpected residue, discoloration, or contamination.
 * Manufacturing output should comply with quality standards, and no orange spots should be visible on the chip surfaces unless explicitly defined and approved by the manufacturing process.
 * {*}The source of the residue should be identified and documented{*}, and its impact on device functionality and long-term reliability should be assessed.

summary: Updater Tool: Downgrade cannot be re-triggered after the FPGA flash step fails
description:
h2. Summary

When a downgrade is started from the newest firmware and the FPGA flash step fails, the device is left half-flashed (FW 1.5.140, FPGA still 1.5.61) and the downgrade cannot be started again: the tool returns to the main screen, which reports FW 1.5.140 as flashed.
h2. Steps to Reproduce

1. Device is on the newest firmware.
2. Make the FPGA flash step fail. Reproduced by modifying the USB interface to mimic a failing FPGA upgrade — the easiest way to provoke it.
3. Start the downgrade with CTRL+D.
4. After the FPGA step fails, try to start the downgrade again.

*Reproducibility:* yes, with the modified USB interface. The issue is expected to occur whenever the FPGA upgrade times out; this has not been confirmed on unmodified hardware.
h2. Expected Result
 * Device is left half-flashed: FW 1.5.140, FPGA still 1.5.61 (accepted outcome of the failed FPGA step).
 * The failed downgrade can be re-triggered.

h2. Actual Result
 * Device is left half-flashed as expected: FW 1.5.140, FPGA still 1.5.61
 * The downgrade cannot be re-triggered — the tool is back on the main screen, which shows FW 1.5.140 as flashed.

h2. Environment
 * *Tool:* firmware update tool (CTRL+D downgrade shortcut) — exact tool name and version not recorded
 * *Firmware before downgrade:* 1.5.165
 * *State after failed downgrade:* FW 1.5.140, FPGA 1.5.61
 * *Reproduction setup:* USB interface modified to mimic a failing FPGA upgrade

h2. Impact

The device stays on a mismatched FW/FPGA combination, and the tool offers no path back to a consistent state because it treats FW 1.5.140 as successfully flashed. 
h2. Workaround

Upgrade again to 1.5.165. and retry the downgrade to 1.5.140.

summary: Integration Test Plan for Firmware (1.5.165-RC7) and Updater Tool (3.2.4101.11137-RC7)
description:
h1. Purpose of this Document

This document defines the Integration Tests to be performed in the context of the CAPA release of the firmware and the Updater Tool for the USB3 Interfaces. It covers Firmware (1.5.165-RC7) and Updater Tool (3.2.4101.11137-RC7) as well as a new golden image 1.5.61.

A broad pool of PCs with varying hardware configurations (see chapter Hardware Configurations) is used across these tests to also cover hardware variance. This is especially relevant for the IOSS Smoketests, which are fully repeated on 6 different PCs with different hardware setups.
h2. Test Breakdown
 * *Updater Tests* - executed in [Y3839-668|https://jira.dentsplysirona.com/browse/Y3839-668] on all PCs of the test hardware pool below, except C0006-MFGPROD18.
 * *Firmware Tests* - executed in [Y3839-667|https://jira.dentsplysirona.com/browse/Y3839-667], using the same PC pool as the Updater Tests.
 * *Production Firmware Upgrade* - executed in [Y3839-670|https://jira.dentsplysirona.com/browse/Y3839-670], performed on a single PC (C0006-MFGPROD18) only.
 * *IOSS Smoketests* - basic customer workflow simulation, executed across the executions listed below.
h3. Updater Tests / Firmware Tests

[Y3839-668|https://jira.dentsplysirona.com/browse/Y3839-668] (Updater) and [Y3839-667|https://jira.dentsplysirona.com/browse/Y3839-667] (Firmware) are executed against the test hardware pool listed below (excluding C0006-MFGPROD18). Note: not every test case is repeated on every system of the pool.

In some tests, the firmware package itself is used directly instead of the AE USB Upgrade Tool - for example when only an FPGA or Cypress update needs to be flashed onto the USB3 Interface.
h3. Production Firmware Upgrade

[Y3839-670|https://jira.dentsplysirona.com/browse/Y3839-670] is executed on a single PC (C0006-MFGPROD18) only. 50 different Remotes at the York production site are upgraded to the new firmware using the AE USB Upgrade Tool (the official name of the Updater Tool).
h3. IOSS Smoketests

The IOSS Smoketests simulate the real-world experience of a customer in the field: the customer first updates the firmware of the Interface Box to the new version, and afterwards continues normal clinical usage, e.g. by performing a single-shot or template exposure.

The firmware is updated from the most common version in the field (1.5.121) to the version under test (1.5.165) using the AE USB Upgrade Tool. Afterwards, a single-shot exposure and a template exposure are performed with a patient; both exposures must complete without errors and without image artifacts. During the template exposure, sensors are exchanged between exposures to simulate a worst-case scenario where a sensor loses connection and has to be reconnected, or where a different/new sensor has to be used - this also verifies the stability of the reconnect / re-plugging behavior. Finally, the test confirms that the sensor and USB3 Interface data (hardware details) can still be read out correctly after the firmware update.

The tests are executed on 4 PCs with Sidexis, 1 PC with Dentrix and 1 PC with Eaglesoft, all with IOSS integration. To cover hardware variance, the full test is repeated identically on each of these 6 PCs, which all have different hardware configurations.

Executions:
 * [Y3839-682|https://jira.dentsplysirona.com/browse/Y3839-682] - IOSS Smoketest Dentrix PCX00039
 * [Y3839-681|https://jira.dentsplysirona.com/browse/Y3839-681] - IOSS Smoketest Eaglesoft PCX00053
 * [Y3839-680|https://jira.dentsplysirona.com/browse/Y3839-680] - IOSS Smoketest Sidexis PCX00154
 * [Y3839-679|https://jira.dentsplysirona.com/browse/Y3839-679] - IOSS Smoketest Sidexis PCX00194
 * [Y3839-678|https://jira.dentsplysirona.com/browse/Y3839-678] - IOSS Smoketest Sidexis PCX00238
 * [Y3839-677|https://jira.dentsplysirona.com/browse/Y3839-677] - IOSS Smoketest Sidexis PCX00239

h2. USB3 Interfaces (Serial Numbers)

All USB3 Interfaces used in these tests carry a serial interface on the board, which is only physically accessible after removing the housing. Some tests include reading out device logs that can only be retrieved via this serial interface. Removing the housing for this purpose is not considered a modification of the USB3 Interface: the housing can be fully restored to its original state at any time, and the serial interface itself is a permanent, unaltered part of the board on every unit - it is only made temporarily accessible, not added or changed.

description:
h2. Description

During an acquisition session in {*}Sidexis with IOSS{*}, the intraoral sensor was unplugged and re-plugged. This resulted in an inconsistent system state with multiple symptoms.
h2. Steps to Reproduce
 # Start an acquisition session in Sidexis with IOSS
 # Unplug the intraoral sensor during the session
 # Re-plug the sensor
 # Observe system behavior
 # Trigger an exposure
 # Repeat exposure multiple times

h2. Observed Behavior

*After sensor reconnect:*
 * The *USB3 interface rebooted multiple times* (LED alternates between orange and green)
 * After some time, the remote became ready and signaled *acquisition readiness*
 * The *IOSS viewport remains red* (no image, no ready state)
 * The *info area in IOSS (bottom)* shows no error message — empty, despite a problem being present
 * In the {*}Intraoral Sensor Configuration App{*}, the connected sensor is *shown twice*
 * In the {*}acquisition phase selection menu in Sidexis{*}, the sensor is also *listed twice*

*After triggering exposures (observed via attached video):*
 * Upon triggering radiation, the viewport shows a *loading animation* and the info text states that image data is being received
 * The image *is actually delivered* successfully
 * After the first image arrives, *the next viewport turns red* in IOSS but with a loading animation. USB interface was ready for exposure.
 * The same image is received several times. Afterwards the viewport turns red without loading animation. 
 * Triggert another exposure, which results in several images received

h2. Expected Behavior
 * After reconnect, IOSS should re-initialize the sensor and set the viewport to ready (green)
 * If an error occurs, the info area in IOSS should display a meaningful error message
 * The sensor should appear only once in the configuration app and the Sidexis selection menu
 * Each viewport should only be filled by an actual exposure — no duplication of the last image

summary: It is possible to acquire images with IOSS without enabling event detection
description:
*Steps to reproduce:*
 # Start IOSS session with Gen 2 sensor via IOSS API
 # Set sensor exposure ready via IOSS API
 # Trigger sensor via light exposure
 # IOSS now automatically picks up the image in the background => sensor is again in state 3 and session has one image
 # Trigger sensor via light exposure => sensor state 5 => 6, IOSS does not pick up the image automatically
 # Set sensor exposure ready via IOSS API (seems to be this is not sent to the device)
 # IOSS now automatically picks up the image in the background => sensor is again in state 3 and session has two images (no checkerboard image)

*Expected result:* 

Image acquisition is only possible when enable event detection is activated 

*Actual result:*

Image acquisition is possible even if event detection is not enabled.{*}{*}

*Note:*
 * The flow above is a miss-usage of the  IOSS acquisition flow and only possible because the sensor is always enabled for event detection (after it is activated once for enabled event detection)
 * It is expected that the checkboard fix will not work for the above flow, even with IOSS.

summary: Unexpected host LED state in non-Sidexis setup
description:
In an environment with only IOSS and a 3rdParty PMS, the USB3 interface host LED is flashing green with long green phase (2x green 1x off). 

IOSS recognizes the USB3 interface and the sensor, BUT without configured Sidexis Server in IOSS, the state on the USB3 interface is not constant green, as expected. 

As soon as an exposure is started, the host LED shows the breezing green. After the exposure it switches back to constant green. 
Disconnecting the sensor in that state, leads to a fall-back to the initial flashing pattern (2x green 1x off). 

+*Customer Impact:*+ 

The USB3 interface does not provide a consistent status indication via the host-LED. Sometimes it is flashing, sometimes it is constant green. Though the situation is the same in every status.

h2. Introduction

This test aims to confirm the compatibility of the USB 3 interface firmware update with the Velocity CDR drivers. The target group of the firmware release 1.5 for the USB 3.0 interface are Eaglesoft users. The firmware 1.5.121 was already rolled out only to Sidexis 4 users with the update of the intraoral sensor plugin version 3.0.4000.60108 and above. Since the update is not available to Eaglesoft user, a standalone firmware update utility was developed. The firmware, that is installed using the update utility, is the focus of this test. This test plan is based on the document SW-339 "Velocity CDR Software Verification Test Plan".
h2. Testing Scope

In addition to the compatibility of the firmware 1.5.121 with the Velocity CDR drivers, the compatibility to Eaglesoft, CDR DICOM, CDR TWAIN and the CDR SDK is also tested.

Eaglesoft in its latest version (22.00.08) supports Windows 10 x64 and Windows 11 64x. 
A standalone workstation of CDR DICOM as well as the drivers for AE and Schick 33 sensors support Windows Pro 10 x64 and Windows Pro 8.1 x64. 
Windows 8.1 shall be excluded from the tests, since the security support is discontinued and therefor can no longer be classified as a secure system environment needed for medical products.
Therefor the only to be tested operating system is windows 10 pro x64.

summary: USB3 Interface Stuck in Red LED State which requires PC Restart to Restore Connection
description:
+*Actual Behavior:*+
The USB interface is unable to establish a stable connection to Dentrix via CDR. Only a PC restart resolves the issue. Dentrix freezes at the "Getting device ready" screen; meanwhile, the sensor LED remains green while the interface LED is frozen in red status.
Dentrix was restarted, the device was unplugged/replugged multiple times, and the CDR app was closed via Task Manager and restarted — the issue persisted.

+*Reproducibility:*+
During an unplug/plug test of the sensor, the device sometimes restarted on its own (LED sequence changing green → red → green), even though it remained connected the entire time. On one occasion, this restart apparently did not complete successfully (sporadic behavior), causing the USB interface to get stuck in this state. Unplugging and replugging the device did not resolve it — only a full PC restart allowed the device to re-establish a stable connection.

+*Additional Information:*+
See logs in attachment. The issue first occurred at 1:55 AM.
Sensor: Xios XG Supreme Gen1: 72012231
USB Interface: 2031530, FW: *1.5.152*

+*Update:*+
The issue could also be reproduced with the new firmware version ({*}1.5.154{*}).

summary: Dentrix/CDR: USB3 interface fails to reconnect to sensor after multiple plug cycles, sensor LED stays orange
description:
h2. Description

After performing several reconnect cycles of the sensor in a *Dentrix with CDR integration* setup, the USB3 interface was unable to establish a connection to the sensor. The sensor LED remained *orange* (no connection), and the system did not recover without further intervention (serveral re-connections of the USB3 Interface).
h2. Steps to Reproduce
 # Start acquisition session in Dentrix with CDR integration
 # Repeatedly unplug and re-plug the sensor
 # Observe the sensor LED after each reconnect

h2. Observed Behavior
 * After several reconnect cycles, the USB3 interface no longer establishes a connection to the sensor
 * The *sensor LED remains orange* — no transition to green/breathing (ready state)
 * The system does not self-recover

h2. Expected Behavior
 * The USB3 interface should reliably re-establish a connection to the sensor after each reconnect cycle
 * The sensor LED should transition to green/breathing (ready state) after a successful reconnect

h2. Additional Information
 * Integration: Dentrix with CDR
 * Trigger: Multiple sensor / USB3 interface reconnect cycles
 * Timestamp in Log around *16:53*

summary: Dentrix/CDR: No image delivered after exposure following ~9 min wait in ready state
description:
After performing an exposure in *Dentrix* (CDR integration), the system completes the capture process but fails to deliver or display the resulting image. The issue occurred specifically after the system had been in the "Ready for Exposure" state for approximately *9 minutes* before the exposure was triggered.
h2. Steps to Reproduce
 # Open Dentrix and perform an initial image capture — succeeds
 # Close and reopen Dentrix
 # Start a template exposure (multiple captures)
 # Complete the first two captures successfully
 # System enters *"Ready for Exposure"* state
 # Wait approximately *9 minutes* without triggering an exposure
 # Trigger the third capture
 # Observe whether an image is delivered

h2. Observed Behavior
 * The first two captures in the series complete successfully
 * After waiting ~9 minutes in the ready state, the third exposure is performed
 * The capture process completes, but *no image is delivered or displayed* in Dentrix

h2. Expected Behavior
 * After a successful exposure, the captured image should be delivered and displayed in Dentrix regardless of how long the system was in the ready state beforehand

h2. Related issues
 * This issue might be related to Y3839-570 where no image was recorded after an exposure was performed in Eaglesoft.

summary: CDR: Sensor remains armed (event detection not disabled) if integrator transitions from State 6 directly to State 3 (Idle) — stray exposures are silently captured
description:
h2. Summary

CDR does not provide a fixed acquisition service like IOSS; instead, Dentsply Sirona ships a DLL that lets third-party integrators build their own control/workflow logic for the USB3 Interface. State 6 is the state in which the USB3 Interface signals to the PC that an image is ready for pickup. Because CDR integrators fully own the workflow, nothing enforces that event detection is disabled (SetEventDetection(False)) once the PC has read out that image: an integrator can transition directly from State 6 to State 3 (Idle) without ever disabling event detection, leaving the sensor armed.

The PC Connection LED cannot be used to detect this: its breathing pattern (LEDCONTROL state 5) is a separate command, only sent once the driver's internal state machine explicitly confirms reaching State 4. If a workflow skips this confirmation (as seen in the attached log), the LED never breathes and gives no indication that the sensor is still armed.

While still armed, any radiation on the sensor produces a new, unattended image (State 5 -> State 6) with no PMS interaction. This stray image is then picked up as soon as the next acquisition phase is opened in the PMS.
h2. Steps to Reproduce
 # Perform an exposure via CDR; the USB3 Interface enters State 6, signaling to the PC that an image is ready for pickup.
 # The PMS reads out the image, then transitions the workflow to State 3 (Idle) without sending SetEventDetection(False) (integrator does not implement disarm).
 # Apply radiation to the sensor while in this state - no PMS interaction, Connection LED gives no indication (not breathing, same as normal idle).
 # The sensor captures a new image (State 5 -> State 6), unattended.
 # Start a new acquisition phase in the PMS - the stray image is picked up.

*Log evidence ({{{}VelocityUSB.log{}}}):* {{SetEventDetection(False)}} is sent only once at session start (08:08:17). From 08:09-08:14, State 5 -> 6 -> 3 repeats several times, re-armed each time via {{SetEventDetection(True)}} with no disarm in between. {{SetLedState(state: 5)}} (breathing) never appears, since no {{State: 4}} confirmation is ever logged for this flow - only {{state: 4}} (non-breathing).
h2. Observed Behavior
 * CDR allows a State 6 -> State 3 transition without SetEventDetection(False), because the integrator fully owns the workflow logic (DLL-based, not a managed service as with IOSS).
 * The Connection LED does not reveal this: breathing depends on a separate confirmation path that this flow never triggers.
 * A subsequent, unrelated exposure is captured and silently picked up on the next acquisition.

h2. Expected Behavior
 * The state machine should not allow State 6 -> State 3 without disabling event detection first.
 * *Recommendation:* enforce this on the firmware side - have the USB3 Interface automatically disable event detection on every State 6 -> State 3 transition, regardless of what the PC/integrator sends. This removes the dependency on correct third-party workflow implementation entirely.

summary: Sensor stays unregistered in Sidexis after 401 on device re-registration (expired refresh token, no retry)
description:
h2. Root Cause
* Sidexis node-authentication refresh tokens expire after 3 days ({{RefreshTokenEncoder.REFRESH_TOKEN_EXPIRATION}}); access tokens after 1 h.
* The long-lived singleton client in {{DeviceRegistrar}} is only used when {{SidexisMonitor}} detects a lost->available transition. If more than 72 h pass between two such triggers (PC only suspended, short reconnect gaps often missed by the 300 s poll; weekends sit right at the 72 h edge), its refresh token is expired: POST deviceRegistration -> 401, library-internal refresh -> 401 ("Expired refresh token").
* {{DeviceRegistrar}} swallows the exception and {{SidexisMonitor}} sets {{LastConnectionStatus=true}} -> no retry until the next detected transition (can be days). The device registration in Sidexis stays stale and the sensor appears disconnected until then.
* Evidence: customer logs of SR 8001491478 (see TPDX5-937) -- all 9 occurrences had >72 h since the last successful registration (closest: 72 h 09 min), all successes <72 h (closest: 71 h 59 min).

h2. Workaround
Restart the Windows service {{SironaUSBService}} ("Dentsply Sirona Intraoral Sensor Service") or reboot the PC (real restart; shutdown with Fast Startup does not restart services). Reinstalling the plugin works only because it restarts the service.

h2. Possible Fix
In {{SidexisApiHelperV6.RegisterOrUpdateDevice}}: on 401, call {{EnsureClientIsAuthenticatedAsync()}} and retry once -- after the failed refresh the token container is already cleared, so this performs a full authentication. Optionally, {{SidexisMonitor}} should retry a failed registration on the next poll.

summary: USB race condition on cold boot causes sensor NoHardware state
description:
{panel:bgColor=#e3fcef}
ℹ️ This content was generated with AI assistance and may require human review.
{panel}
h2. Summary

On system cold boot, two code paths run simultaneously for the same USB device, causing a race condition that leaves the sensor in NoHardware state after startup.
h2. Steps to Reproduce
 # Enable nightly system reboot (or perform a cold boot)
 # Service starts automatically at boot
 # AddConnectedDevices() finds USB sensor immediately and creates VelocityUsbDevice #1
 # Windows sends DEVICEEVENT notification (USB re-enumeration) ~200-800ms later
 # VelocityUsbDevice #2 is created and resets all USB endpoints (0x00, 0x01, 0x81, 0x82, 0x83, 0x84)
 # Endpoint reset interrupts ongoing ReadCalibrationData call on Thread A
 # Try to use sensor for X-ray acquisition

h2. Expected Result

Sensor initializes correctly after cold boot and is available for X-ray acquisition.
h2. Actual Result

Sensor is stuck in NoHardware state. Error in log:
{code:java}
ERROR - SendMessageAndReadResponse (6) - An error occurred reading payload.
        Total bytes received: 0, NtStatus: 0x000003E3, UsbdStatus: 0xC0010000
{code}
Manual service restart is required every morning.
h2. Environment
 * *Application:* IO Sensor Service (SirexisPlugin.ServiceHost) v2.2.2518.4182
 * *OS:* Windows (Korean, Build 9200)
 * *Hardware:* Xios XG Supreme sensor (AE Sensor USB Interface, VID 0FBC PID 0020, Firmware 1.5.121)
 * *USB Driver:* Cypress USB (CyUSB)

h2. Severity / Impact

High — doctor cannot take X-rays every morning until manually restarting the service.
h2. Root Cause

Two code paths fire for the same USB device on cold boot:
 # {{AddConnectedDevices()}} scans for already-connected USB devices at service startup and creates VelocityUsbDevice #1
 # Windows sends a DEVICEEVENT notification (USB re-enumeration after boot) shortly after, triggering DeviceNotificationProvider_OnDeviceAdded which creates VelocityUsbDevice #2

VelocityUsbDevice #2 resets all USB endpoints. If this reset overlaps with an ongoing ReadCalibrationData call from VelocityUsbDevice #1, the I/O is aborted (NtStatus: 0x000003E3 = ERROR_IO_OPERATION_ABORTED).

Log signature:
{code:java}
[Thread A] Creating VelocityUsbDevice ...   <- from AddConnectedDevices()
[Thread A] Device status changed to available
[Thread B] Creating VelocityUsbDevice ...   <- from DEVICEEVENT, ~200-800ms later
[Thread B] Resetting endpoint 0x00 / 0x01 / 0x81 / 0x82 / 0x83 / 0x84
[Thread A] Reading calibration data from sensor now...
[Thread A] ERROR - NtStatus: 0x000003E3, UsbdStatus: 0xC0010000
{code}
Note: The race condition is timing-dependent. If the endpoint reset finishes before ReadCalibrationData starts, no error occurs (lucky timing). This explains why it does not fail on every cold boot.
h2. Why It Only Affects Cold Boot

On service-only restart (no system reboot), AddConnectedDevices() does not find the device via CyUSB scan — only the DEVICEEVENT delivers it. Therefore only one VelocityUsbDevice is created, no race condition.
h2. Proposed Fix

In {{DeviceNotificationProvider_OnDeviceAdded}} (VelocityDeviceListener.cs): if the device already exists in the manager list and no suspend/resume cycle has occurred, do *not* create a new VelocityUsbDevice and do *not* reset USB endpoints. The endpoint reset should only happen on actual USB disconnect/reconnect (physical or after suspend/resume).
h2. Workaround

Configure a Windows Scheduled Task that restarts the service on user login with a ~30 second delay. Since this is a service-only restart (not cold boot), the race condition does not occur.
h2. Evidence

Siroforce support ticket 8001417365 (customer "Bonsu", Korea, Windows Build 9200).
Log files analyzed: SensorPluginService.log (2026-03-23 to 2026-03-26).
 * 2026-03-24: Race condition occurred but timing was lucky — no failure
 * 2026-03-25 08:46: Race condition with overlap — calibration read failed, sensor broken all morning until manual restart at 09:15

summary: Remote signals sensor connection even tokens are not received any more
description:
h2. Description

In the current design there are two possible mechanisms to indicate a good remote to sensor connection.
 # Path: Sensor present signal -> this is currently checked
 # Path: periodically sent TOKENS from the sensor to the remote -> this is currently not checked. 

If the data lines (D+/D-) from the sensor to the remote are disconnected, the sensor is still powered and the sensor present is still connected to the remote, the remote and Sidexis does not visualize the data line interruption correctly. Because everything shows a proper working system the customer will trigger the XRay, but no image will be transfered from the sensor to the remote. *Result: Lost Image.*
h2. Steps to Reproduce
 # Connect the sensor to the remote
 # Start Sidexis and go to the acquisition mode
 # PC-LED on the remote is breathing green and sensor-LED is constantly green. Sidexis window is breathing green, too
 # Tilt the sensor in that way that D+/D- are not connected any more
 # PC-LED on the remote is breathing green and sensor-LED is constantly green. Sidexis window is breathing green, too
 # Trigger X-Ray
 # No image will be shown in Sidexis

h2. Observed Behavior
 * If we are in the acquisition mode and the data lines from sensor to remote are interrupted, the system do not inform the user about this problem  
 * The user triggers X-Ray without getting an image

h2. Expected Behavior
 * When the system indicates it is ready for acquisition, the image must arrive in the acquisition software after the radiation is triggered.

h2. Additional Informations

See confluence page: [Error handling/visualization issue - Intra-Oral X-Ray - Confluence Dentsply Sirona|https://wiki.dentsplysirona.com/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=409929170]

summary: Synergy/Raptor USB Interface Module Self-Resets and Disconnects During Acquisition (reproducible only on the USB 2.0 box, not the USB3 Interface)
description:
h2. Summary
The XIOS XG legacy "Synergy" USB interface module (VID_0FBC&PID_0004, Blackfin BF533 + NET2272 -- a USB 2.0 device, NOT the USB3 Interface/Velocity product) repeatedly crashes and self-reboots via its own watchdog during normal image-acquisition series. Root cause identified at firmware source level: the firmware treats a wide range of internal conditions as fatal and force-resets via WDTimerActivate(), and several USB-command handlers wait with no timeout at all, which can leave the module deaf on USB before a secondary trip-wire eventually reboots it. This has NOT been reproduced on the USB3 Interface (Cypress FX3-based) product -- it is specific to the legacy USB 2.0 box.

h2. Steps to Reproduce
* Connect an XIOS XG Supreme sensor to a legacy Synergy/Raptor USB 2.0 interface module (VID_0FBC&PID_0004, "USB Interface", firmware Raptor.sldr, field-deployed version 2.38).
* Perform a rapid series of exposures (e.g. a full-mouth/Zahnstatus series), one image every few seconds.
* Observe the module after roughly every 5-15 images (field median ~10).

h2. Expected Result
The module keeps answering USB status/image requests continuously across the whole series; exposure readiness stays available between images.

h2. Actual Result
* After a successful image readout, within a few seconds (field median: 4 s) the module either:
  (a) drops off the USB bus instantly (Windows PnP surprise removal) and re-enumerates about 3.2 s later -- matching the firmware's own watchdog timeout, or
  (b) stops answering GetStatus/write requests first (a deaf period, field median 9.5 s, observed up to several minutes) before eventually dropping and re-enumerating the same way.
* Host-visible symptoms: exposure readiness drops to "not ready", both LEDs on the module go dark, Sidexis/IOSS logs show "Failed to read Status." / "Failed to write GetStatus request." followed by a device-removal/re-arrival pair for VID_0FBC&PID_0004.
* Not reproduced with the USB3 Interface (PID_0020, Cypress FX3) product in the material reviewed -- appears specific to the legacy USB 2.0 (Synergy/Raptor) box.

h2. Environment
* Application: Sirona Sidexis4 sensor plugin 3.1.3120.49190 / Sidexis 4.4.1.2, IOSS.
* Hardware: XIOS XG legacy "Synergy" USB 2.0 interface module (VID_0FBC&PID_0004), firmware Raptor.sldr v2.38 (Blackfin BF533 + NET2272), paired with XIOS XG Supreme sensors (sensorTech 19).
* Not reproduced on: the newer USB3 Interface / Velocity product (Cypress FX3, PID_0020).
* Field occurrence: Poliklinik Bonn, 2 workstations, 529 crash episodes over 78 clinic days (full field-log analysis in linked ticket).

h2. Severity / Impact
High workflow impact at high-throughput sites: field data shows a roughly constant 5.5-9% crash probability per image, which at a university-clinic series workload (150-300 images/day/bay) produces 5-15 visible failures per day per bay. No corrupted-image reports were found in the material reviewed (unconfirmed whether specifically checked). Patient-safety/regulatory relevance of repeated exposures is a QM/RA decision, not addressed here.

h2. Workaround
None at the software/field level -- cable, module, and sensor-head swaps do not change the crash rate, since the defect is in the module firmware itself, common to the whole module generation. The module usually self-recovers (re-enumerates) within seconds to a few minutes without user action.

h2. Logs / Attachments
See linked ticket TPDX5-931 for the full field-log analysis (529 episodes, both workstations). Root cause detail (source: cdr repo, CDRHardware/Xray/Synergy/SynergyRemote/application/RaptorG2/):
* ~50 internal error conditions (enum REBOOT_ERROR_CODES, RAPTOR.h) each call SchickErrorHandler() -> WDTimerActivate(), forcing an immediate watchdog reset (RAPTOR.cpp). One trigger is a single flicker of the sensor-present status bit (SENSOR_CONNECTION_CHANGE in SENSOR_G2_INTERFACE.cpp), which the code's own comment flags as needing softer handling ("TBD make it softer, like send a status to Host") -- never implemented.
* Several USB-command handlers wait forever with no timeout (PendSemaphore(kSENSOR_THREAD_DONE_SEMAPHORE, 0), 6+ call sites in Host_Interface.cpp) while a separate thread keeps servicing the watchdog on its own schedule -- this produces the "deaf" period seen before some resets.
* The trigger window is the module's own post-acquisition housekeeping: G2/Supreme sensors send a keep-alive token roughly every 20 ms; a gap over 100 ms (G2_TOKEN_TIMEOUT, RAPTOR.h) forces an internal sensor power-cycle recovery sequence, which is where the error trip-wires above get reached.
* Diagnostic note: the firmware already reports its own crash reason across the reset (usb_status.error_code, Core_Module.h) in every status packet, but the host plugin does not currently read or log it (see the "Reserved" field of USB_STATUS in SchickTypes.cs). Logging it would attribute every future crash to a specific internal cause with no firmware change required.

Accuracy note: the checked-out firmware source (cdr repo, git-svn mirror of SVN trunk, no tags) is at version 2.34.3106 at HEAD; the field-deployed module is confirmed at v2.38 (four point releases later). The mechanisms above are confirmed in the 2.34-era source and inferred, not byte-for-byte verified, to still apply at 2.38.

summary: Remote and sensor stuck in ready, not switching to ready-for-exposure
description:
A customer (reproduced on a visit of Gregor Schmitt / Werkskundendienst) complained about a sensor not getting ready for exposure after several unplug / plug-in scenarios. The LEDs on the IO remote are both constantly lit in green, in IOSS the viewbox is flashing red. 

At the Bensheim lab I was able to reproduce the issue if the sensor was not connected properly (not entirely plugged in an slightly bend to the side). 
From logs in that case it seems as if the IOSS does not initiate the ready4exposure state on the IO remote for an unknown reason. 

*In General:* 
 * The state does not lead to falsely performed exposures (both IOSS and IO remote do not show a ready state)
 * Restarting the IOSS acquisition session does not help
 * Restarting the IOSS service does not help

 * Restart of the IO remote is required => most likely a firmware issue.

+*Reproduction at Bensheim [NikFou]*+

With 1.5.140, it occurred once during sensor 20 re-connections. The problem persisted until the remote was reconnected. In the event of an error, the sensor LED still turned green again each time it was reconnected, but in IOSS the viewport no longer turned green.
